newsitem.title: UK: British Gas to sell North Sea gas fields.
newsitem.headline: British Gas to sell North Sea gas fields.

text.p: British Gas Plc will sell its interests in several North Sea gas fields as part of disposals which could net up to 500 million pounds in cash, the Observer newspaper said on Sunday.

British Gas is in the process of a demerger and the paper said the sales would be overseen by BG Plc, the rump of the company made up of its exploration and production division as well as domestic pipeline network TransCo, the paper said.
The Observer quoted BG chief executive David Varney as saying this was "a new chapter" in the firm's strategy.
It said Varney would be reviewing all BG's exploration and production before April and intends hiving off "non-core" assets, while declining to say which fields were likely to go.
Varney told the paper a straightforward sale was possible, but there might be a swap. It said the group wants to increase the proportion of oil in its portfolio.
The Observer said the Brae field, which is seven percent owned by British Gas, would be top of the list, with other possible candidates the Audrey, Beinn, East Leman, Maureen and Moira fields.
The paper said Varney accepted that the fields in which BG has small stakes could be sold but added that other factors could play a part.
"It depends on the rate of return and whether we believe they are a springboard for other things," the paper quoted him as saying.

The Observer also reported that British Gas customers in one part of the country could pay more than others as part of a new gas pricing plan. It said this was in response to the opening up of competition in the domestic gas market.
The paper said Roy Gardner, chief executive of Centrica -- the domestic gas supply arm which is to be demerged this week -- confirmed he would discuss its options with the industry regulator.

"We are going to offer a whole range of payment options which will give customers better choice to suit their needs, there will be new tariffs to suit particular circumstances," the paper quoted him as saying.
It also said Gardner had confirmed that Centrica, which has already branched into financial services with launch of its Goldfish credit card, would shortly be offering insurance.
Gardner plans to settle outstanding take-or-pay liabilities for gas by the end of the year and will not sell all the Morecombe gas fields in northwest England, the paper said.
He also indicated "that although an ordinary dividend was unlikely before 1999, an earlier special dividend or share buy-back could be possible", the paper added.
